stem: Air temperature is near target, but one dense canopy zone remains humid with weak air movement and recurring localized stress. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Evaluate airflow distribution, heat removal, moisture removal, canopy density, and local plant response together rather than assuming room-average temperature proves adequate environmental control.
Add fans without measuring the affected zone because fan quantity determines airflow quality.
Ignore humidity because temperature is on target.
Use the room-average RH to rule out localized moisture conditions.
rationale: Environmental control depends on distribution and interacting heat/moisture removal functions; acceptable averages can hide localized boundary-layer or airflow problems.
